rows.label: Share of All Hands and Hearts' programme spending outside the US (year to August 2025)
rows.explainer: Our judgment: neither the audited statements nor the Form 990 split programme spending by country (the 990 files no Schedule F). The 990's three largest programmes, all in the US (Hurricane Helene in North Carolina $2,700,913, Helene and Milton in Pasco County, Florida $2,364,662, the Los Angeles wildfires $1,363,557), are 51% of its $12,523,438 of programme expenses; the other $6,094,306 covers the Texas floods (from July 2025), other US responses, programme staff and volunteer support at headquarters, and the programmes abroad: school rebuilds in Nepal (Bandevi School) and the Philippines (two schools), 17 classrooms repaired in Oaxaca, Mexico, and the Myanmar earthquake response from Thailand (13,000 people). Costed bottom-up those come to about $1.2 million (a Nepal school about $250,000, All Hands and Hearts' own campaign figure of $5 million for 20 schools; bamboo schools in the Philippines and classroom repairs in Mexico less; relief at about $40 a person), $1.5-3 million with country staff, bases and travel: 18%, from 10% to 30%. Read by both All Hands and Hearts models, so the two always split the programme spending in full.

source.title: All Hands and Hearts Smart Response, Inc., Form 990 for the year to 31 August 2025 (public disclosure copy)
source.page: Part III lines 4a-4e, p. 2; Schedule O
